title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The current generation, continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming. Key model IDs as of mid-2025:

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4 |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Balanced |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Current default Sonnet |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Most capable; also powers Claude Code Fast mode |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision.

---

## Claude 4.7 → 5 Generation (Late 2025 – 2026)

The naming scheme shifted again: instead of incrementing version numbers within a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus tier, Anthropic introduced a fourth tier name, **Fable**, for its top frontier releases, alongside an internal-only **Mythos** line.

- **Claude Opus 4.7** (late 2025) powered Claude Code's Fast mode — Opus-level output delivered faster.
- **Claude Code Security** launched February 20, 2026 as a limited research preview (public beta April 30, 2026), using Opus 4.7 to scan entire codebases for vulnerabilities by reasoning about data flow rather than pattern-matching against a CVE database. Findings go through a multi-stage verification pass to cut false positives before a severity rating is assigned.
- **Claude Opus 4.8** shipped May 28, 2026, becoming the most capable model in the 4.x line.
- **Claude Fable 5** was announced June 9, 2026 — Anthropic's most capable widely-released model at launch, state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks across software engineering, knowledge work, vision, and scientific research. **Claude Mythos 5** launched alongside it as a specialized (not publicly released) model used by a consortium of companies to find software vulnerabilities.
- **Export-control interruption:** On June 12, 2026, the US government applied export controls to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 after Amazon researchers found a jailbreak that got Fable 5 to produce exploit code for a vulnerability it had identified. Access for foreign nationals was restricted until the controls were lifted June 30. Fable 5 was redeployed July 1 with new classifiers to better block cybersecurity misuse, restored across the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.
- **Claude Sonnet 5** launched June 30, 2026, billed as "the most agentic Sonnet yet" — able to plan, drive a browser and terminal, and run autonomously at a level that previously required Opus-class models, at Sonnet pricing ($2/$10 per million input/output tokens through August 31, 2026; $3/$15 standard thereafter).
- **Claude Opus 5** followed July 24, 2026: a frontier-class agentic-coding and computer-use model at unchanged Opus pricing ($5 input / $25 output per million tokens). It has a 1M-token context window (both default and maximum), up to 128K output tokens, and extended thinking on by default with a selectable effort dial (low/medium/high/xhigh/max). It matches or beats Fable 5 on most public benchmarks at roughly half the input price, and leads outright on agentic coding (Frontier-Bench) and novel reasoning (ARC-AGI-3).

**Current lineup (as of August 2026):**

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest tier |
| Sonnet 5 | `claude-sonnet-5` | Most agentic Sonnet; Opus-adjacent capability at Sonnet pricing |
| Fable 5 | `claude-fable-5` | Frontier reasoning and broadest general capability |
| Opus 5 | `claude-opus-5` | Agentic-coding and computer-use flagship; 1M-token context |

*(The mid-2025 table further above — Sonnet 4.5/4.6, Opus 4.7 — is kept for historical reference; those model IDs have since been superseded by the lineup above.)*

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K tokens (stable Claude 2.1 through the 4.x line) → **1M tokens** with Opus 5
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use (now standard on frontier/agentic tiers)
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → four names (Haiku / Sonnet / Fable / Opus), with version numbers reset to "5" across the family in mid-2026
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing — Sonnet 5 explicitly targets Opus-class agentic behavior at Sonnet prices
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems; thinking effort is now a first-class, selectable dial rather than an on/off toggle
- **Safety/export policy:** Frontier models can now be subject to export-control action after deployment (the June 2026 Fable 5/Mythos 5 episode), not just at launch review
